answer: Each identity claims one glacier lantern tower and posts a 75-credit bond tied to its trellis lamp frame. Each epoch the keeper files lamp-hours with a fuel log, and auditors recompute fuel burned per lamp-hour from the public tower log; a reused frame serial, a copied fuel entry, or burn outside a 3% tolerance burns the bond. The first tower costs 33 credits, the k-th 33+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5028 and 1000 fakes pay 2,530,500 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-lantern ring fails: one lamp cannot burn fuel in two towers at once. An honest keeper pays 33 once for one tower.
